title: Diagnostics gap for priority pathogens
bottleneck: WHO's 2025 analysis found critical gaps in diagnostics for priority bacterial pathogens: tests to rapidly identify resistant infections and guide therapy are unavailable or unaffordable where resistance is worst. Without point-of-care diagnostics, clinicians prescribe empirically, accelerating resistance and mistreating patients.
why_it_blocks: Diagnostics are the steering wheel for both stewardship and surveillance; without them, antibiotic use is blind and resistance tracking is guesswork. The pipeline fixation on drugs while ignoring diagnostics guarantees misuse of whatever drugs arrive.
current_state: WHO released paired 2025 reports on antibacterial and diagnostic pipelines, both warning of shortfalls. Rapid molecular tests exist for a few pathogens but have not reached low-resource settings at scale. Multiplex point-of-care panels that identify pathogens and resistance genes in one test exist as prototypes, but cost and cold-chain needs block deployment where resistance is worst.
